name: Snakes
label: Dischord
lede: Two Georgetown kids from SOA made a goofy pop record so far from hardcore that Dischord put it out under a fake label name, then did it again five years later.

eras.title: The band before the bands
eras.text: Michael Hampton and Simon Jacobsen grew up together in Georgetown, and the Snakes were their private joke that ran underneath everything else. Dischord says the band both predated and co-existed with their hardcore bands.

years.h: Michael Hampton and Simon Jacobsen start the Snakes
years.p: [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Simon Jacobsen|59d87a31-7ad6-418f-bee0-5a4738acf357]] already have the Snakes going in Georgetown when they start playing in The Extorts, Hampton's first band on record.

years.h: Michael Hampton and Simon Jacobsen play on [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]]'s No Policy
years.p: Hampton on guitar and Jacobsen on drums play on SOA's No Policy, Dischord No. 2, fronted by Henry Garfield before he was [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]]. Hampton moves on to [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] with [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]].

eras.title: Welcome to Discard Records
eras.text: In 1985, the year of Revolution Summer and the most earnest season DC punk ever had, Dischord released fourteen songs of playful, proto-punk-flavored pop. The label was nervous enough to change its own name on the sleeve.

years.h: I Won't Love You ('Til You're More Like Me) · Dischord No. 18
years.p: The Snakes' debut: fourteen songs recorded at Inner Ear Studios, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and the band. Titles include Snake Rap, Serv-Pro Joe and License to Fish.
play: I Won't Love You ('Til You're More Like Me)

years.src: Dischord · Bandcamp Daily · End On End
years.h: Dischord releases the Snakes as Discard Records
years.p: The Snakes' debut album goes out under the name Discard Records, a tongue-in-cheek cover for Dischord's strangest record yet.
years.xp:
Writing for Bandcamp Daily, Tony Rettman says Ian MacKaye and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] worried how people would react to Dischord releasing something so puckish, so they swapped the name. Rettman traces the sound back to proto-punk rather than hardcore.

An End On End podcast episode with Simon Jacobsen, recorded for Dischord's 40th anniversary, called the Snakes an anomaly in the scene and especially on Dischord.

years.h: The Snakes' only show: the 9:30 Club
years.p: The Snakes are a recording project. They play live exactly once, at the 9:30 Club, with two friends Dischord names only as Brendan and Guy as backing musicians.

eras.title: Happy, and a second disguise
eras.text: Michael Hampton kept moving through the post-Revolution Summer bands while the Snakes stayed a studio habit. Their second album, Happy, came out in 1990, co-released with Adult Swim Records, a small D.C. label.

years.h: Michael Hampton joins One Last Wish
years.p: After [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], Michael Hampton plays in [[One Last Wish|94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8]] with three former members of [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]]. Wikipedia places the Snakes alongside it, rarely playing live.

years.h: The Snakes' Happy · Dischord No. 50.5, with Adult Swim
years.p: The Snakes' second album: thirteen songs co-released by Dischord and Adult Swim Records, including My Girl Gloria, Oh No, Olga and Dance, Mr. Fish. A listener on Dischord's page calls it catchy bubblegum pop with cheesy keyboards.
With Ivor Hanson and [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]], Michael Hampton starts Manifesto, which puts out an album and a 7" and gets noticed in the UK.

eras.title: Dug back up
eras.text: Both Snakes records went out of print, then turned up on Bandcamp and in a new round of Dischord deep-cut lists. Michael Hampton, meanwhile, was playing power pop in Fake Names with a band full of old friends.

years.h: Michael Hampton's power-pop band Fake Names
years.p: Michael Hampton's [[Fake Names|a4271e33-8969-4dd8-9e3c-88b269e89fe0]] brings in [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]], Johnny Temple, Dennis Lyxzén and [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]]. Hampton has also spent years scoring TV, games and film.

years.h: Simon Jacobsen on the End On End podcast for Dischord's 40th
years.p: Simon Jacobsen talks through the Snakes' first album on End On End's three-hour-plus episode, alongside Dot Dash's Hunter Bennett, as Dischord marks its 40th year.

years.h: Bandcamp Daily calls the Snakes a Dischord hidden gem
years.p: Bandcamp Daily's list of Dischord records beyond [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] leads with the Snakes and the story of Dischord disguising itself as Discard Records.
